_doc: OPEN-STANDARDS-1 (Rowan 2026-11-25): "Standards, don't reinvent the wheel ... Audit everything and refactor it with standards and autonomous closed loops." Settings of the supply-chain loop: OpenSSF Scorecard and the SPDX SBOM GitHub's dependency graph exports are read weekly by .github/workflows/supply-chain.yml, summarised by `python3 -m foundation supplychain --ingest` into ops/supply-chain.json, and every Scorecard check under the floor or SBOM package outside the licence policy becomes a Q-STD-SC-* item whose closing probe is `supplychain --probe`. The standards themselves are entries in seed/standards/standards.json.

ignore_checks.Code-Review: CLOSED-LOOP-1: changes are reviewed by automated checks and a different agent, not by a person approving a pull request
ignore_checks.Contributors: measures outside organisations contributing; not something the system can change by code
ignore_checks.CII-Best-Practices: the OpenSSF Best Practices badge is a self-assessment form filed in the owner's name
ignore_checks.Maintained: counts recent human activity; machine commits are the maintenance here
ignore_checks.Signed-Releases: no release artifacts are published; deploys go straight to Workers
ignore_checks.Packaging: nothing is published to a package registry
ignore_checks.Fuzzing: OSS-Fuzz admission is an outside programme; tracked as a standards entry, not a weekly item
